liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls the exploratory middle section of Shakedown one of the best such noodling stretches of any version; Agrees with another reviewer about the incredible exploratory section of Shakedown [20][23][29][31]
- **China Doll** (3 reviews): China Doll is a welcome inclusion but feels hurried; The Playin' jam flows beautifully into China Doll, following Shakedown Street [20][24][29]
- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Reviewer rates the Morning Dew as very good; Morning Dew is called monumental [20][22][29]
- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): The second-set stretch before Drums is said to leave listeners grinning; The Wheel leads into a Playin' reprise, which then goes into Morning Dew [21][24]
- **Bertha//** (1 review): Reviewer complains that Bertha is played too fast [25]

## Setlist highlights

- **Playin Jam followed by Weir Improvisations with Hart/Kreutzmann**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **Fire**: rare: 13 archived performances [32]
- **Estimated**: rare: 13 archived performances [32]

## The recordings

- **gd83-05-14.senn.fishman.15387.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1983-05-14.176405.senn421.blend.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 137 min [4]
- **gd1983-05-14.168030.beyer.m201.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 138 min [6]
- **gd1983-05-14.163384.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 136 min [8]
- **gd83-05-14.sennheiser.gustin.342.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 18 songs; 137 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [12]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is so strong the reviewer rechecked the source; it is nearly soundboard-like, an audience tape at a sweet spot; Audience recording so clean it sounds like a soundboard; reviewer compares its quality to the 3-25-83 tape; Recording is good enough, though the sound is somewhat wavy at times [21][22][23][24][25][26]
- **gd83-05-14.set1-sbd.samaritano.25407.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 49 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [18]

## Around the show

- Attendee calls it their most memorable Dead show; they took two hits of acid and felt it intensely during the opening Stranger [23]
- Reviewer says the Greek often brought out the band's best, and this show fits that pattern [21]
- Reviewer finds the show much better than 3-25-83, though the tapes are of similar quality [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-05-14.senn.fishman.15387.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jeff Silberman; transferred by DAT(fostex d10)>CDR>DAE (via EAC)>CDR-WAV (for Tracking)>MKW>SHN encoded by Jeff Fishman, via Dougal Donaldson; source: FOB: Sennheiser 421's > Sony PCM-F1 [1]
- **gd1983-05-14.176405.senn421.blend.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics (x3) > Sony PCM F-1 > Sony D5 (patched out of Dave Kramer & Matt Field) [4]
- **gd1983-05-14.168030.beyer.m201.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ken Kelley; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ken Kelley's Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M201 mics > JVC KD-2 w/Super ANRS (Maxell XLII-S90) [6]
- **gd1983-05-14.163384.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Jim Vita's 1st Generation Cassettes [8]. Also: Patches come from a Nakamichi 700 source (first 0:05 of Bertha) and a Sony ECM220t source (1:06 in Drums) [8]
- **gd83-05-14.sennheiser.gustin.342.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB: 3 Sennheiser 421's > Sony PCM-F1, M. Field, D. Cramer [12]
- **gd83-05-14.set1-sbd.samaritano.25407.sbeok.shnf**: source: *Set 1 Only* Soundboard->Cassette Master->1st Generation Cassette. 1st Generation Cassette->Audiophile 2496->Samplitude v7.02… [18]. Also: The first-set soundboard is the only board source from the weekend; nothing circulates from Friday [27]

Audience recording so clean it sounds like a soundboard; reviewer compares its quality to the 3-25-83 tape
Reviewer finds the show much better than 3-25-83, though the tapes are of similar quality
Morning Dew is called monumental
Recording is good enough, though the sound is somewhat wavy at times
Attendee calls it their most memorable Dead show; they took two hits of acid and felt it intensely during the opening Stranger
Agrees with another reviewer about the incredible exploratory section of Shakedown
The Playin' jam flows beautifully into China Doll, following Shakedown Street
The Wheel leads into a Playin' reprise, which then goes into Morning Dew
Sound is excellent, leaving listeners unsure whether it is soundboard or audience
Reviewer complains that Bertha is played too fast
Reviewer finds Jerry's first-set solos sound poor on this recording
Reviewer considers it one of the better audience recordings, though Brent is a bit low in the second set
The first-set soundboard is the only board source from the weekend; nothing circulates from Friday
Jerry forgets lyrics early in Shakedown; Bobby and Brent cover and make it a credible version
After China Doll, Brent plays a synth part while Jerry plays a spooky lead in the jam
Morning Dew is a highlight following the post-drums Weir improvisations
Reviewer praises the vocals in the Shakedown outro
Recorded with Sennheiser 421 microphones into a Sony PCM-F1, from Jeff Silberman's PCM master, encoded by Jeff Fishman
Master cassettes came from Scott Wiseman, with transfer coordinated by Charlie Miller, using a Sennheiser 421 blend source
Dave Kramer and Matt Field's Sennheiser 421 source patches 0:42 of China Doll and 0:10 of Sugar Magnolia
Beyer M201 recording from Ken Kelley's master cassettes, transferred by Charlie Miller; a Sennheiser 421 source patches 0:12 of Drums > Space
Nakamichi 304 recording from Jim Vita's first-generation cassettes, transferred by Charlie Miller
Patches come from a Nakamichi 700 source (first 0:05 of Bertha) and a Sony ECM220t source (1:06 in Drums)
